text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- A special meeting of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's cabinet held in Islamabad on Friday was told that there were 400 terrorists and 800 proclaimed offenders involved in violent crimes and subversive activities in Punjab province and elsewhere in the country.

- The Pakistan Air Force has said spread of population in funnel areas of airfields and inadequate garbage disposal facilities have contributed to an increase in birds in the vicinity of airfields posing a serious threat to flight safety.
- Pakistan's four provinces have sought an additional amount of 500 million rupees from the federal government within the next two months to cope with any emergency in case of river floods.

- Federal Minister for commerce Ishaq Dar informed the National Assembly on Friday that the budget deficit in the fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) would further swell by 40 billion rupees from the expected shortfall of 60 billion.
- The Privatisation Commission has decided not to accept any guarantee for payment for any privatised enterprise and will now privatise the remaining state-owned units for cash.

- The Pakistan Investment Fund, a closed-end country fund, has posted a return of 19.5 percent compared to 18.9 percent for the Karachi Stock Exchange's 100-share index for the quarter ending on March 31, 1997.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, at his cabinet meeting on Friday, described sectarian terrorism in Pakistan as an extraordinary situation that needed to be handled on war footing.

- President Farooq Leghari, while talking to Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain in Islamabad on Friday, held India's RAW intelligence network and other anti-Pakistan forces responsible for sectarian violence and called for a clean-up operation against terrorists.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has expressed his concern over poor revenue collection as the government faces a shortfall of more than 50 billion rupees in the current financial year.
- In the wake of deteriorating law and order situation in Punjab province, law-enforcing agencies have suggested to the government to suspend cellular telephone services in the province.
- Police throughout Punjab province launched a massive crackdown on activists of militant sectarian outfits on Friday and arrested 83 people.

- Pakistan Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said in an interview with the state television on Friday that normalisation talks with India could come to a deadlock if New Delhi did not agree to discuss a solution to the 50-year-old dispute on Kashmir.
THE NATION
- The government has decided to set up an anti-terrorist task force to uproot terrorsim and escalated sectarian violence in the country.

- The Pakistani government will replace the present obsolete and corruption-prone revenue collection machinery with a new one dominated by the private sector. The decision was taken at a meeting Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif held in Islamabad on Friday with economic managers of the government and representatives of trade bodies.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Pakistan's annual development plan for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) has been conceived with a gross domestic product growth rate of 6.0 percent and inflation at 9.0 percet, with investment projected to grow to 530.8 billion rupees.
- The Privatisation Commission has decided to dispose of as many as 15 industrial and commercial units before the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 to get some short-term recoveries.

- The government has planned to borrow foreign funds in the commercial market and intends to raise commercial foreign currency loans to the tune of $115 million upto June, said Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
